column1: # THE FLEET. One row per class, smallest to largest. Tab separated, so a blurb can hold commas and
# apostrophes freely. Edit here (or in a spreadsheet, exported as TSV), then:
#     npm run import && npm run catalogue
# Lines starting with # are ignored, so notes and section breaks are fine.
# THE GAMEPLAY COLUMNS. These are what the fight and the shipyard read.
# id          a short camelCase name, unique. Becomes the key everything else refers to.
# name        what a captain reads. Sentence case, no em dashes, no interpuncts.
# price       coins to buy the bare hull. 0 for the ship she starts with.
# hull, crew  maximum health in the same points the bars already use. Hull is the reference's own
#             timber formula; crew is her battle complement, floored at 25 because a crew bar is a
#             health bar and a dozen points is four musket balls.
# speed       her own pace before a stitch of canvas, off her working speed under sail.
# hand        how she answers her rudder, before canvas. From the reference's handling components
#             less the rig and the crew: her sails carry the rig half themselves.
# canvas      how much sail she WANTS to get moving, as displacement to the two thirds. The most
#             important number here: it is why a half-rigged big ship is genuinely bad, and why the
#             same suit drives a cutter hard.
# tons        what she carries before her guns start telling on her handling. Set so a class with the
#             heaviest iron in every port sits at her limit, and moved by how fine she is: a beamy
#             hull carries her guns better than a sharp one.
# broadside   guns A SIDE, mirrored. bow and swivel are totals.
# masts       where she can step one, "station/size", space separated, bow aft.
#             stations: bowsprit fore main mizzen bonaventure
#             sizes:    boat small medium large heavy
#             The bowsprit takes a SPAR rather than a mast, which is what her headsails hang on.
# bowsprit    yes or no. Whether she carries the spar at all.
# blurb       one line a captain reads. May be left empty.
# THE REFERENCE COLUMNS. Everything from `era` rightward is what the class WAS rather than what she
# does in a fight: nothing reads it, `npm run import` writes it to src/shipref.js, and it is there
# for whoever comes to model the hulls. Lengths are feet and weights are tons; bowFine, tumblehome,
# deadrise, sheer and castle are 1 to 5 judgement scores, 1 for least and 5 for most.
